title: 数量＋は — “at least (amount)”
summary: When the particle は follows an amount (time, number, quantity), it means “at least that much.” The speaker feels the actual amount is that or more. It is usually followed by verbs like かかる, ある, 入る.

patterns.form: 数量（＋助数詞）＋ は ＋ かかる／ある／V
patterns.gloss: amount + は = at least that much (三日は, 百人は, 一週間は)

body.p: Here は is the particle of contrast. Putting は on an amount points to that amount as a minimum line: “that much, at the very least (and maybe more).” Nothing special is added to the number itself: 三日は, 百人は.
It is often used with expressions of time needed (かかる), capacity (入れる) or existence (ある), and with guess forms such as だろう and そうだ. It is a natural estimate, not an exact count.
三日以上 is a plain, objective “three days or more.” 三日は carries the speaker's feeling or judgment, such as “it'll take three days, I'm sure.”

examples.ja: この仕事（しごと）は三日（みっか）はかかります。
examples.romaji: Kono shigoto wa mikka wa kakarimasu.
examples.tr: This work will take at least three days.

examples.ja: この会場（かいじょう）には、百人（ひゃくにん）は入（はい）れるだろう。
examples.romaji: Kono kaijō ni wa, hyakunin wa haireru darō.
examples.tr: This venue can hold at least a hundred people.

examples.ja: 完成（かんせい）までに、あと一週間（いっしゅうかん）はかかりそうだ。
examples.romaji: Kansei made ni, ato isshūkan wa kakarisō da.
examples.tr: It looks like it will take at least another week to finish.

pitfalls: は goes right after the amount. Do not use it for an exact or fixed number: 「ちょうど三日は」 sounds wrong.
It expresses a minimum guess. To say the opposite (at most), use ～しか or ～まで instead.
